input: The staffing position on the document-control side has, unfortunately, become more difficult than had previously been expected, largely because the contract checker who had been carrying the EPC review load left the project before a cleared replacement had been appointed to take over the work. As a result, a staffing gap of 6 weeks is now reported, and during that period the checking sequence for the affected packages cannot be staffed in the way that had originally been planned. It is important to note that the gap is not presented as a general shortage across the whole project; rather, it sits in a specific checking function, and it is the concentration of the work in that function that makes the absence difficult to absorb. In terms of a response, it is proposed that the checking load for the affected packages be redistributed to cleared home-office reviewers for the duration of the gap, and the project board is proposed as the owner of that redistribution, so that the decision and its follow-through rest in one place. This would not remove the underlying shortage, but it would keep the review sequence moving while the replacement is brought into post, and it would avoid each affected package making its own separate arrangement.
target: A staffing gap of 6 weeks is reported in EPC document control. The contract checker who carried the review load left the project before a cleared replacement had been appointed, and the checking sequence for the affected packages cannot be staffed as planned during the gap. The gap sits in one checking function rather than across the project, and the concentration of the work in that function is what makes the absence difficult to absorb: packages that depend on the same checker queue behind one another, and partial cover by staff without the clearance does not release them. The mitigation is a redistribution of the checking load for the affected packages to cleared home-office reviewers for the duration of the gap. The project board owns the redistribution. Ownership by the project board puts the decision and its follow-through in one place, and affected packages do not make separate arrangements. The mitigation does not remove the shortage. The shortage ends when the replacement is in post and cleared; until that point, the redistributed load keeps the review sequence moving at the cost of drawing on home-office capacity that was assigned elsewhere. Cover of this kind is workable because the home-office reviewers hold the same clearance as the checker who left, and the packages affected are those already in the review sequence rather than new work entering it. Work not yet in the sequence waits for the replacement, and the distinction keeps the mitigation bounded: the redistributed load is the load the gap would otherwise have stalled, and no wider commitment is made. The reported position is therefore a six-week gap in a single function, a named cause, and one mitigation with a named owner.
